primitives.note: Baleful Strike, Dark Matter, and Primordial Burst each deal magic damage on cast (Q immediate, W after a 1.2s impact delay, R via projectile) on their own cooldowns.

Phenomenal Evil Power: each enemy-champion hit by an ability grants 1 stack (+1 AP), a takedown grants 5 more; stacks are uncapped and never expire, so AP (and thus Q/W/R damage) ramps over the fight as abilities land on the dummy.

Dark Matter's cooldown is not the flat per-rank value (bin lists 0 for all ranks); it starts at a base of 8s and steps down by a factor of 0.9 each time 50 Phenomenal Evil stacks are accumulated, so W's cast frequency depends on how fast stacks build during the fight.

Primordial Burst's damage is amplified 1.5% per 1% of the target's missing health, capped at 66.66% missing health for a 2x (max) multiplier; against a full-health dummy this starts at minimum damage and ramps as the dummy is damaged.
The 2x max-damage multiplier is only reached once the target is at or below one-third remaining health, functioning as a soft execute threshold worth timing R around.

Event Horizon deals no damage (damagetype is blank, spelleffects blank); its only effects are stun/knockdown, which a damage-only dummy fight never reads. It may still be worth casting purely to trigger a Phenomenal Evil stack (see unsettled).

needsBespoke.why: Q/W/R damage-on-cast, the passive's stack-based AP buff, W's stack-gated cooldown reduction, R's missing-health damage scaling/execute cap, and E's damage-free status are all expressible with existing primitives (plain-cast, stacking-self-buff, cooldown-manipulation, conditional-damage, execute-or-threshold, defensive-only). No unique engine logic is required beyond combining these.

unsettled.question: Does casting Event Horizon at a stationary dummy actually register as an ability 'hit' for Phenomenal Evil Power purposes, given the ability's stun/knockdown only trigger on units crossing the cage edge and a stationary dummy standing at the cage center may never cross it?
options: The dummy is treated as hit/affected by the cast regardless of movement (per 'abilities do not have to deal damage nor affect their targets to grant a stack'), so E generates a passive stack every cast
The dummy never crosses the cage boundary and so is never 'hit', meaning E generates no stack and is pure dead time/mana cost in the fight
quotes: '''Veigar's''' abilities do not have to deal damage nor affect their targets to grant a stack.
Enemies that collide with the edges of the cage are {{tip|knockdown|knocked down}} and {{tip|stun|stunned}} for a duration.

unsettled.question: How exactly does Dark Matter's stack-gated cooldown formula (base 8s, x0.9 per 50-stack threshold) resolve within a single 15s fight where stacks are actively accumulating mid-cooldown — is the applicable cooldown for a given cast determined by stacks at the moment W was last cast, or does an in-progress cooldown get shortened retroactively the instant a 50-stack threshold is crossed?
options: Cooldown length is fixed at the value implied by current stacks when W is cast, and does not change again until the ability is off cooldown
Cooldown updates live: crossing a 50-stack threshold mid-cooldown immediately shortens the remaining cooldown to match the new (lower) total cooldown
quotes: {{pp|type=[[File:Phenomenal_Evil_Power.png|20px|link=Veigar#Phenomenal_Evil_Power]] [[Veigar#Phenomenal_Evil_Power|Phenomenal Evil]] stacks|8*0.9^(x-1);...;0|0 to 900 for 19;...;∞|formula=8 * 0.9^N. ''N{{equals}}Number of times that 50 Phenomenal Evil stacks are earned.''}}

unsettled.question: For ordinary ability-hit stacks (as opposed to kill-triggered stacks, which the wiki explicitly says apply 'on next game tick'), is there any similar tick delay before the +1 AP from a hit applies, which would matter for whether a spell's own hit can boost its own damage calculation or only later casts within the same 15s window?
options: Hit-based stacks (and their AP) apply instantly/synchronously with the hit, so even later hits in the same frame/cast see the updated AP
Hit-based stacks apply with the same 'next game tick' delay described for kills, so AP updates only affect subsequent casts, not anything resolving in the same instant
quotes: The stacks are added immediately on enemy kill (on next game tick).

proposal: Open by casting Baleful Strike (Q) and Dark Matter (W) back to back (each has only a 0.25s cast time) to start generating Phenomenal Evil Power stacks and begin damaging the dummy.

Continue casting Q on its short cooldown (4-6s by rank) and W whenever it comes off cooldown (reduced over time as Phenomenal Evil stacks accumulate) to build burst damage and drive the dummy's health down as fast as possible.

Hold Primordial Burst (R) until the dummy's remaining health is at or below roughly one-third (i.e. missing health at or above the 66.66% cap), then cast it to land at the maximum 2x damage multiplier; given R's long cooldown (60-120s by rank), only one cast is realistically available in a 15s window, so timing it for the cap is a pure gain.

Fill all remaining time with Q on cooldown and W on cooldown; do not cast Event Horizon, since it deals no damage and its value (a possible passive stack) is unsettled and likely marginal compared to spending the cast time/mana on Q or W instead.
questions: Is Event Horizon worth casting purely for the Phenomenal Evil stack (and its +1 AP) against a stationary dummy, or does it never actually register as a 'hit'?

At what specific stack counts (given expected cast frequency of Q/W/passive triggers over 15s) does Dark Matter's cooldown actually drop below its 8s base, and does that reduction apply retroactively mid-cooldown or only to the next cast?

Should R be delayed to hit the 66.66%-missing-health cap even if that means it lands later in the 15s window, or is casting it as early as possible (accepting a lower multiplier) better for total kill time given the simulator's fixed fight length?
